## Mirror a reflecting wall (`reflecting`) {#sec-ch11-reflecting}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Copies the $n_g$ owned cells next to the wall into the ghosts in reversed order and negates
the normal momentum or velocity row; every other row keeps even parity.

**Switch.** Face name `reflecting`; the default of every external face.

**Requires / implies / turns off.** Nothing. The WB wall treatment of @sec-ch11-wb and the corner refresh of
@sec-ch11-timing both act on faces that carry this callback.

**Order.** Exact for data that is even (odd) about the wall; no wall convergence order is measured.

**Defining equation.** @eq-ch11-reflecting-parity.
:::

The reflecting callback is the symmetry wall of the solver: a sealed boundary through which the normal mass
flux vanishes by reflection symmetry of the Riemann problem. It is the default face name of the card, so a
block without a `boundary-condition` entry has six reflecting faces. The callback is pure mirror arithmetic on
the supplied tensor; whether that mirror is a good continuation of a stratified column is the question
@sec-ch11-wb answers.

### Derivation

Use only cell averages here. At a Cartesian lower wall let the first owned cell have index $i$ and let
$l=1,\ldots,n_g$ count ghost depth. Integrating an even extension of a scalar over each reflected cell gives
its matching owned-cell average. Integrating an odd extension of normal velocity gives the negative average.
For an orthogonal wall, density is even and normal momentum is odd, so their ratio has the same odd parity.
Thus the callback implements

$$
\begin{aligned}
q_{i-l}&=q_{i+l-1},\\
v_{1,i-l}&=-v_{1,i+l-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-reflecting-parity}

Here $q$ is any even component and $v_1$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
The upper-wall mapping reverses the last owned slab in the same way. `reflecting_inner`
([`bc_func.cpp:10-34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L10-L34))
and its upper-wall twin `reflecting_outer` implement @eq-ch11-reflecting-parity with a `flip` of the adjacent
slab and a sign change of the row `4-dim`, which is the normal velocity row of the dimension being filled
(`dim` 3 is x1, so row 1 is `IVX`).
At a symmetry-preserving Riemann interface, equal densities and opposite normal velocities give zero normal
mass flux by reflection symmetry. This argument does not supply a hydrostatic pressure continuation or a
proof for arbitrary nonorthogonal component conventions. Check C1 verifies the exact discrete parity and the
idempotence of a second fill [check `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`]. The checks do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The input stays in its supplied representation. Conserved and primitive calls negate the normal row;
a `kScalar` call only mirrors, so a tracer density or a limiter factor keeps even parity. A collapsed
direction (one cell) returns at once. The fill runs with the physical fills of @sec-ch11-timing, before
reconstruction consumes the ghosts, and again on the exchange-owned tangential slabs after an exchange. The
odd/even extension is exact for data that has that symmetry; no measured wall convergence order is available
here.

@fig-ch11-reflecting-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch11-reflecting-stencil
#| fig-cap: "Mirror a reflecting wall. Schematic only; no simulation measurements."
#| fig-alt: "Labelled schematic of the reflecting boundary operation; ghosts and owned cells have separate text labels."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch11.fig_reflecting_stencil import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Implementation sites for reflecting. {#tbl-ch11-reflecting-code}

1. Return for a collapsed direction, then copy and reverse the adjacent owned slab of width $n_g$. The anchor
   `reflecting_inner` is in
   [`bc_func.cpp:10-34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L10-L34).
2. Negate the normal row for conserved or primitive input; keep even parity for scalar input. The anchor
   `reflecting_outer` is in
   [`bc_func.cpp:10-34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L10-L34).
3. Repeat on the exchange-owned tangential corner slabs after a block exchange. The anchor `refresh` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}.

Device/rank distinctions and missing runs are recorded in @sec-ch15-ch11.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A mirror of the total state is not a continuation of a stratified equilibrium: the mirrored pressure rises
into the ghosts of a lower wall where the hydrostatic column would fall. The reference-state procedure of
@sec-ch11-wb addresses that distinction for the x1 reconstruction. Reflection alone establishes neither the
accuracy of wall diffusion coefficients nor a nonorthogonal momentum treatment.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
